topic: PostgreSQL roles, policies and privileged code
title: PostgreSQL roles, policies and privileged code
brief: Test PostgreSQL privilege and row-policy boundaries as the actual application roles.
outcomes: Explain role inheritance, ownership and policy bypass
Secure privileged routines against identity and name-resolution mistakes
entry: General least privilege and tenant boundaries (RL104), including application connection ownership. The needed secure deployment, SQL object names and session identity are introduced locally.

heading.title: Roles and ownership
heading.brief: Pin a secure owned PostgreSQL deployment and introduce the connection identity, database, schema, named objects and SQL session needed for these tests. Create separate runtime, migration and support roles; test memberships, object privileges, default privileges and sequence access on pinned PostgreSQL.

heading.title: Tenant policies
heading.brief: Apply shop_id row policies and test read and write checks; show owner, superuser and BYPASSRLS behaviour and the effect of forced policies.

heading.title: Identity on a pooled connection
heading.brief: Distinguish authenticated role, SET ROLE and trusted tenant context; reset connection state and reject a spoofed caller-supplied tenant.

heading.title: Privileged code
heading.brief: Exercise a SECURITY DEFINER routine with controlled search_path, schemas and execution grants; demonstrate a denied name-shadowing attempt and protect ownership.
